info.title: DataGround API
info.description: Native DataGround contract for isolation-scoped agent-service discovery, immutable revisions, invocations, event replay, approval resolution, cancellation, and artifacts. Additive changes are compatible within v1. Removing or renaming fields, narrowing accepted values, changing state or error semantics, or making optional fields required is breaking and requires a new major API version. Clients must ignore unknown response fields and unknown event types while preserving the event envelope. All versioned API operations require a bearer access token whose issuer, audience, and isolation-domain membership are validated before a deployment authorizer evaluates the principal, closed action, path-derived resource identity, and effective isolation domain.

get.summary: List agent services in an isolation domain
get.description: Returns one bounded newest-first page. The opaque cursor continues from the last item without widening isolation scope.

get.summary: List revisions for an agent service

post.summary: Create an immutable service revision draft
Retire an unrouted and inactive published revision
post.description: Atomically retires a published revision after checking its expected version, absence of aliases, and absence of nonterminal invocation or publication activity. Retirement prevents new routing and operator repair through this revision. It retains resource history, artifacts and audit; it does not delete content or replace retention policy.

get.description: Reads one isolation-scoped revision by immutable identifier, including its current publication or retirement state. No newest-revision or alias fallback is performed. The request requires readServiceRevision authorization on that exact revision.

post.description: Both input and output schemas must compile without external resource loading before publication is accepted. Invalid contracts return non-retryable 409 REVISION_INPUT_SCHEMA_INVALID or REVISION_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_INVALID without schema details.

200.description: A page of active service aliases

get.description: Returns active aliases ordered by name in ascending ASCII order, with a default limit of 50 and maximum of 100. Cursors bind the exact isolation domain and service; each request is independently authorized. Withdrawn aliases are excluded. Pages reflect current routing state rather than a frozen snapshot; assignment, withdrawal, or recreation may change later pages. Refresh from the first page to reconcile concurrent changes.

put.summary: Assign an alias to a published revision

post.description: Stops new routing through this alias after an exact version check. Accepted invocations and historical command replay remain unchanged. The response records withdrawnAt; ordinary alias reads return 404 while withdrawn. Assigning the name again uses the absent-alias precondition (omitted or zero expectedVersion) and preserves its identity while advancing its version, preventing stale updates after reuse.

get.summary: List invocation summaries for a service
get.description: Returns a bounded page ordered by creation time and identifier, newest first. Cursors bind the exact isolation domain and service; each request is independently authorized. Summaries exclude inputs, results, error payloads, usage and artifact contents. Later pages reflect current lifecycle state; this is not a frozen snapshot.

post.summary: Invoke a published service revision through an alias
post.description: New invocations validate input against the exact alias-resolved revision inputSchema before creating work. JSON Schema defaults to draft 2020-12; external resource loading is disabled. Input mismatch returns 400 INVOCATION_INPUT_INVALID; an invalid or unresolvable schema returns 409 REVISION_INPUT_SCHEMA_INVALID. Accepted idempotent replay retains the original revision and response after alias changes. Reference runtimes validate the completed result against that revision outputSchema; invalid output ends as failed with INVOCATION_OUTPUT_INVALID and no result, while an invalid retained schema uses REVISION_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_INVALID. This is a terminal invocation outcome, not an admission rejection.

get.description: Returns the provider-neutral durable state of one approval already identified by the invocation event stream. The invocation path is matched before the resource is disclosed, and adapter-native identifiers remain private.

post.description: Resolves one provider-neutral durable approval after both API action authorization and exact revision-bound invocation authorization succeed. The route never exposes adapter-native identifiers, and an exact idempotency replay returns the originally committed response.

get.summary: Replay the invocation event journal as server-sent events
get.description: The Last-Event-ID header is an invocation-local sequence cursor. Unknown event types and fields remain replayable and are safe to ignore.

200.description: Ordered event replay after the supplied cursor.

schema.description: Each data field contains one EventEnvelope JSON value.

200.description: Artifact metadata. Content retrieval is added with the object-store boundary.

BearerAccessToken.description: OIDC/OAuth access token. The deployment-owned authentication boundary validates issuer, audience, credential state, and isolation-domain membership before request processing.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Opaque caller key scoped to the isolation domain, HTTP method, and route. Reuse with a different body fails with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED.

resourceId.description: The exact affected resource in metadata.isolationDomainId: a revision for service-publication or an invocation for invocation-execution. Present on current operation reads and newly accepted publication receipts. Historical idempotent receipts may omit it; clients must obtain an authorized operation read and validate its resource binding before relying on those receipts.

source.description: Trusted event origin class. Runtime lifecycle events describe a native turn and do not establish terminal platform invocation state. Durable reads derive this value from retained journal provenance without changing event identity, sequence, type, or payload. Older envelopes may omit it.

type.description: New event names use dot-separated segments. The exact historical lifecycle.cancellation-requested name remains valid for retained replay; new cancellation requests use lifecycle.cancellation.requested.
